problem_statement: The paper frames credit fraud detection in digital finance as increasingly difficult because fraud is becoming more complex while transaction volumes and real-time payment systems are growing. It argues that existing rule-based and machine-learning systems are not sufficient for modern fraud patterns and need smarter, adaptive, real-time approaches.
problem_statement_quotes: The evolution of the financial ecosystem into a fully digital, globally connected infrastructure has introduced immense efficiency gains, but it has also dramatically increased the complexity and sophistication of fraud.
classical_baseline: The paper treats traditional rule-based fraud detection and conventional machine-learning models as the baseline. It also explicitly compares against a traditional machine learning baseline model trained only on historical fraud datasets, including a random forest model.
classical_baseline_quotes: Traditional financial systems, once reliant on batch processing and human verification, now support billions of transactions per day across digital wallets, mobile banking platforms, peer-to-peer lending services, and decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems.
Rule-based fraud detection systems, while still in use, are fundamentally reactive.

classical_difficulty: The paper says classical approaches struggle with novel and evolving fraud, depend on labelled data, are vulnerable to adversarial manipulation, cannot generate realistic synthetic data for rare fraud types, and face latency and scalability issues in high-frequency environments. It also says imbalanced datasets lead to high false negatives, and black-box models are hard to interpret for compliance.
classical_difficulty_quotes: Rule-based fraud detection systems, while still in use, are fundamentally reactive. These systems flag transactions based on predefined rules or thresholds, but struggle with novel fraud scenarios and evolving tactics.
Traditional models typically require 60–100ms per inference due to the need to scan historical patterns and transaction rules.
business_stakes: The paper says real-time fraud detection is a technical and strategic imperative for banks, fintechs, and regulators, and that false positives can cause customer dissatisfaction and transaction friction. It also notes that fraud can cost institutions billions annually and that deployment must align with compliance frameworks such as PCI-DSS and GDPR.
business_stakes_quotes: In this context, real-time fraud detection has become both a technical and strategic imperative for banks, fintechs, and regulators (Jeyachandran, 2024; Mahmudul Hasan & Faruq, 2025).
This imbalance leads to high false negatives and undetected fraud, which can cost institutions billions annually (Mara et al., 2025).
Traditional ML models suffered from high false positive rates, which may lead to customer dissatisfaction and transaction friction.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit and repeated across abstract, introduction, and conclusion; paper is partly conceptual but still states clear baseline and difficulty framing.
